query: How do reasons for visit relate to urgency and visit duration across department and age group?

per_column.name: visit_complexity
per_column.rationale: A complexity axis could genuinely help relate reasons to urgency/duration. But the distribution is near-degenerate (222/250 'High') and the samples confirm this: a routine annual physical with only mild fatigue and a viral URI with supportive care are both labelled 'High', which the source text does not support. The value is effectively constant and mis-grounded.

per_column.name: symptom_category
per_column.rationale: A clinically meaningful categorisation of reason_for_visit is exactly the new grouping axis the query needs. However groundedness is compromised: the annual physical exam with fatigue is labelled 'pain' though no pain is mentioned, a clear misread. Other samples (infection, chronic_condition, skin) are sound. Mixed reliability.

per_column.name: has_procedure
per_column.rationale: Whether a procedure occurred is a reasonable new axis that could correlate with duration/urgency. Grounding is shaky: the acne visit (topical/oral medication only, no procedure) is marked 'Yes', which the text does not support; the knee case with MRI 'ordered' is arguably a procedure yet marked 'No'. Inconsistent extraction.

judge.rationale: All three columns offer legitimate new axes (complexity, symptom type, procedure presence) that would help relate reasons to urgency and duration, so analytical usefulness is fairly high, though visit_complexity is weakened by being near-constant. Source groundedness is the main weakness: multiple sampled values are mislabelled (physical exam tagged 'pain' and 'High' complexity, acne tagged 'has_procedure=Yes'), indicating the operator frequently asserts readings the source text does not warrant.
